extra.message: Server-Side Request Forgery via Webhook target_url — An attacker can probe internal network services, access cloud metadata endpoints, or attack other internal systems potentially leading to data exfiltration or lateral movement. [verified: The create_webhook endpoint validates only the URL scheme (http/https) but does not restrict the host, allowing an admin/manager to set a target pointing to internal IPs (e.g., localhost:5432). No compensating control (e.g., IP filter, URL parsing) is present in the provided code; the subsequent webhook trigger will make an HTTP request to that attacker-controlled URL.]

Sensitive data exposure via logging of Authorization header — Leak of authentication tokens/API keys to logs, potential account takeover if logs are compromised. [verified: The endpoint logs the raw Authorization header (line 58) to application logs without any redaction, and the code path is reachable by any request that passes the x-internal-token gate. No sanitization or masking is applied, so bearer tokens are exposed to log storage.]

Hardcoded Demo Credentials in Frontend — An attacker can log in as any demo user, including admin, obtaining full access to the application and its data (user PII, lease details, payment records, etc.) [verified: Frontend Login.jsx displays hardcoded demo credentials (lines 53-56) which are trivially retrievable from the client-side bundle; no server-side control prevents an attacker from using them to authenticate as admin, manager, worker, or tenant.]
